principles: Language-neutral by construction: classification is driven by a config-resolved policy, never by hardcoded TS/proofbound-layout assumptions
Single source of truth: one HEAD+materialHash-bound snapshot threaded to all three consumers; no consumer re-derives its own classification
Fail closed: malformed materialCode config and manifest-covering exclusions are rejected with named-key diagnostics, never silently degraded to TS-only
Preserve whitelist direction: unknown and doc formats stay non-material forever
Pure evaluators stay pure: resolution happens once at the transition boundary that has projectRoot
drivers: This is gate code: silent under-classification invisibly disables repro-first RED and review floors for entire language ecosystems
Cross-ecosystem manifests must be non-excludable at level 1, or a single config key can hide backend/go.mod and re-open the hole
Repo compatibility: this repo's execution-time classification delta must be exactly the agreed experiments/ exclusion set (2506 files)

options.name: Per-consumer language lists (patch each of the three call sites independently)
cons: Three lists drift apart over time — reproduces the original bug shape
Project config still cannot reach collectMaterialCodeFiles (the dropped-projectRoot call remains)
ProofStory trigger predicate still never classifies

options.name: Config-resolved resolveMaterialCodePolicy(projectRoot) service + hash-bound snapshot threading (plan v4)
pros: One choke point: floor, repro, and ProofStory all consume the same snapshot resolved once per transition
8-step precedence chain with a level-1 immutable manifest set resists config gaming (two-layer enforcement)
Strict fail-closed resolver surfaces misconfig instead of silently degrading
Snapshot embeds HEAD+materialHash so consumers detect drift and re-resolve
cons: Wider mechanical diff: 3 consumers plus orchestrator threading
Snapshot currency must be re-checked at every consuming gate

options.name: Full per-language semantic support (parsers for py/rs/go/java)
pros: Deepest possible analysis, semantic anchors for every language
cons: Does not fix the classification choke point any better than the policy service

chosen: Config-resolved resolveMaterialCodePolicy(projectRoot) service + hash-bound snapshot threading (plan v4)
rationale: The v4 architecture survived three cross-host audit rounds (codex + agy APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES) and fixes the shared choke point exactly once: policy and diff classification resolve at the transition boundary, an immutable HEAD+materialHash-bound snapshot threads into floor + repro + ProofStory so their decisions can never diverge, level-1 immutable manifests make the fix un-gameable by config, and the strict resolver fails closed. Per-consumer patching reproduces the drift that caused the bug; new language parsers are an explicit non-goal.

preMortem.trigger: The broadened defaults or the level-1 immutable manifest set classify files material in a docs-heavy repo where nearly every story is prose-only
preMortem.consequence: Every docs story would trip repro-first RED and inflate review floors, grinding documentation work to a halt
preMortem.mitigation: Whitelist direction is preserved — unknown/doc formats stay non-material at precedence steps 4 and 8 — and the repro-first classifier keeps its docs/refactor/chore type exemption; the execution-time repo regression check pins this repo's delta to exactly the experiments/ set

preMortem.trigger: A typo in a project's lattice.config.json materialCode block (malformed extension entry, non-string path) after the strict resolver lands
preMortem.consequence: Config-resolve refuses, blocking every story transition in that project until the config is fixed
preMortem.mitigation: Resolver diagnostics name the offending key and value so the fix is immediate and config-only (edit or delete the key — no code rollback); the resolver ships with its own smoke matrix covering malformed-entry shapes

preMortem.trigger: A long validation or a concurrent commit moves HEAD/materialHash after the classification snapshot was computed
preMortem.consequence: Floor, repro, and ProofStory could silently decide on different trees — inconsistent required/floor decisions inside one transition, the exact inconsistency this story exists to remove
preMortem.mitigation: The snapshot embeds the HEAD + materialHash it was computed at; every consuming gate re-checks those hashes at decision time and re-resolves on drift; all three consumers receive the SAME snapshot object resolved once per evaluation, so drift is detected uniformly

preMortem.trigger: Classifying the full main...HEAD diff — 2500+ experiments/ files in this repo — on every gate evaluation
preMortem.consequence: Noticeably slower validate and story transitions for large-diff stories
preMortem.mitigation: This repo's config excludes experiments/ at precedence step 3, and the snapshot is computed once per transition and reused by all three consumers instead of per-gate re-classification
